facts.text: Fredonia, once called Freedona or Hursts Store, hosts the New Hope Rosenwald School, a National Register landmark.
Incorporated September 29, 1853, Fredonia grew into the county’s trade hub, featuring sixteen businesses and the Southern Military Academy.
After the Creek ceded the land in 1832, settlers quickly founded Fredonia, becoming Chambers County’s northeastern pioneer community.
The Fredonia Methodist Church, built in 1833, remains a historic landmark with many early settler descendants still living nearby.
Fredonia enjoys a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers peaking around 89°F and mild winters averaging 33°F.
The town sits on the Southern Piedmont Upland, where rolling hills rise between 700 and 850 feet above sea level.
